scope: Owner decisions of 25 Oct 2026: Spacetoon Classics (ayam-tayebeen) gains Detective Conan and three more top series, shown first in the topic, with the topic's series limit raised from 10 to 14; Kids Riddles gains 10 riddles (30 to 40) and the three phase-2 kids updates. Card ids are kept; new cards take the next free id of their topic. Held categories are untouched.

ownerDecision.spacetoon: Add Detective Conan plus three other top series to Spacetoon Classics and show these four first. The owner approved 14 series for this topic.
ownerDecision.kidsRiddles: Add 10 kids riddles: 30 (12 easy / 8 medium / 10 hard) to 40 (about 14 / 13 / 13), with no very-advanced level.

reviewStatus: pending editorial review; a passing validator or AI review is not factual or bilingual approval
reviewNote: Claude (an AI) wrote or converted every card, opened the sources listed for each card, and checked the Arabic against docs/content-review/ARABIC-STYLE-GUIDE.md (clear Modern Standard Arabic, no dialect). No human editor has reviewed these cards; every card keeps review status pending. Dub names come from Arabic encyclopaedia pages about the dubs (areq.net, 3rabica.org, marefa.org); where those pages and the original disagree, the card gives the dub name first, as the topic already does for Captain Majid. Facts that could not be confirmed on an opened page are listed under unverified. The Detective Conan cards were written in phase 2 (change set g3-nostalgia-anime-fandom, held by the 10-series limit) and converted to Modern Standard Arabic here; the kids-riddles operations come from phase-2 change set g5-puzzles-math (held because the kids content review is bound to the legacy riddle source) and were converted to Modern Standard Arabic here.

swaps.reason: Heidi has a well-known Arabic dub, but no source found that Spacetoon aired it: it is missing from Wikipedia's list of Spacetoon programmes (which lists all ten existing series of this topic, Detective Conan, Hunter × Hunter, Digimon Adventure and Sindbad), and the Arabic encyclopaedia pages say only that it aired on "several Arab stations". The topic is Spacetoon Classics, so the swap the owner allowed was used: Sindbad (Arabian Nights: Sinbad's Adventures), aired by Spacetoon from 2000 and dubbed with Arabic names (Yasmina, Haytham).

question.en: I can carry a giant ship on my back, but I can't hold up a tiny nail. What am I?

added.reason: New medium trick question that teaches why the Moon has phases. Answer shortened so it stays concise.

question.en: Which is heavier: the full moon or a thin crescent moon?

answer.en: Neither: it is the same Moon, lit differently by the Sun.

unverified.note: Kaito Kid's all-white outfit is his well-known look, but none of the opened pages states it; they confirm the dub names and that he announces each theft in advance.

Hunter × Hunter questions call the exam «امتحان القنّاصين», after the dub's title «القناص»; the Arabic encyclopaedia pages write «امتحان الصيادين». The exact dub wording was not confirmed. It affects question wording only, not answers.

Killua's chocolate, his yo-yos and Gon's giant fish are confirmed on the Hunter × Hunter wiki for the story in general; no opened page confirms that each scene appears in the 1999 series the Arabic dub used (62 episodes plus 8 OVA episodes).
The Arabic spellings كايت (Kite) and جزيرة الحوت (Whale Island) are translations; no opened page gives the dub's own forms.
Sonia Bitar as the singer of the Arabic theme rests on one source (areq.net).

Aladdin's lost magic lamp and the old witch's fear of mice come from the English Wikipedia description of the original series (the witch is Tabasa there; the Arabic pages name an old witch ميساء). No opened page confirms that the Arabic dub keeps both details.
The Arabic pages say «نسرين أبيضين»; نسر can mean eagle or vulture, and the English answer says eagles.
Spacetoon's broadcast of Sindbad (2000–2014) rests on Wikipedia's list of Spacetoon programmes; the Arabic pages say only that several Arab stations aired the dub.
